en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Pāricchattaka Tree, from the Section on Female Vimānas.
6. The Story of the Daddalla Mansion “Shining with beauty and illustrious with fame,
you are renowned.”
Among all the Tāvatiṃsa gods,
you outshine them in beauty;
I do not recall ever seeing anyone like you.
“This is the first time I have seen you.
From which body have you come,
and why do you address me by name?”
“O Bhaddā, in a former human existence, I was Subhaddā;
I was your wife at that time.”
And my younger sister—
having passed away from there, with the breakup of the body, I am now fully liberated.
“...have been reborn in the company of the Nimmānarati devas.
“Having performed many deeds of merit, they have been reborn there.”
Those living beings go to the devas,
Subhadda, whose own birth you will praise.
Now, by what quality or by what instruction, and by what kind of giving, have you been guided?
Renowned for her observance of the precepts,
she attained such fame and achieved vast distinction.
“O deity, being questioned, tell me:
what is the fruit of this karma?
“Eight alms-meals indeed...”
That gift which I gave in the past,
with my own hands, full of faith, to the Saṅgha worthy of offerings.
"Because of that, my complexion is such as this...
and my complexion shines forth in all directions."
“I satisfied you with food and drink, O many bhikkhus,
who are self-restrained and lead the holy life.”
With my own hands, full of faith,
I gave even more than you;
yet, I have been reborn in an inferior body.
How is it that by giving so little,
you have attained such vast distinction?
O deity, being asked, tell us.
“Of what action is this the fruit?
“O monk who is so pleasing to the mind,
you were a dear friend to me in the past.”
I invited him for a meal,
with Revata as the eighth person; he, having my welfare as his primary concern, [accepted].
Out of compassion for Revata,
he said to me, "Give [this] to the Sangha," and I acted upon his word.
That gift, having gone to the Saṅgha,
is established upon the immeasurable;
what was given by you to individuals—
“That is not of great fruit for you.
“Only now do I know that what is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.”
Having gone to the human state,
being generous and free from stinginess,
I shall give gifts to the Saṅgha.
“Being heedful, again and again.
“Who is this deity, Bhaddā,
who is consulting with you?”
“He outshines all the Tāvatiṃsa gods in beauty.
“When he was a human being, O Lord of Devas, ...”
In a former human existence,
I had both a wife and a younger sister.
“Having given gifts to the Saṅgha,
one who has performed merit shines forth.
“In the past, sister, by means of the Dhamma...”
With that, O Bhaddā, she shines forth,
because she established an offering within the Sangha, which is immeasurable.
"For on Mount Vulture Peak, I questioned the Buddha regarding the ripening of sharing."
Where a gift yields great fruit for people who are making offerings—
living beings who are seeking merit.
The Buddha explained to me that merit consisting of the acquisitions of the world, when given there, bears great fruit.
Knowing the fruit of one's own action,
[he knows] the ripening of sharing,
wherein what is given bears great fruit.
The four who have entered the path and the four who are established in the fruit—
this is the Saṅgha, upright.
Established in wisdom and virtue,
for those people who are making offerings—
living beings who long for merit.
Merit consisting of the fruits of material offerings,
when given to the Saṅgha, yields great fruit;
for this Saṅgha is vast and sublime.
They are immeasurable like the oceanic sea;
for these are the best disciples, heroes among men,
who radiate light as they proclaim the Dhamma.
Well given, well offered, well sacrificed is that gift which people give dedicated to the Saṅgha;
that offering, having reached the Saṅgha, is firmly established.
Of great fruit and praised by the knowers of the world—
those born of the Vedas who wander the world recollecting such a sacrifice as this.
“Having removed the stain of stinginess along with its root, the blameless ones go to the heavenly state.
The Sixth: The Radiant Mansion.
